headline: Approved consent agenda; discussed Simpson Court mural, train station redevelopment, and economic development incentives
summary: The Economic Development Commission heard presentations on the Simpson Court mural project and on economic development team roles from Dale Kroop of REX Development. Committees reported on the Plan of Conservation and Development, a Manufacturing Day event, and staff activities. The Commission continued discussing current economic development incentives with no final action taken.
decisions: Approved the Consent Agenda, including the September 14, 2026 meeting minutes and September 2026 monthly expenditure reports, by unanimous vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Commissioner Casper made a motion to approve the Consent Agenda. Vice Chair Apuzzo seconded the motion. Consent Agenda was unanimously approved.

a. Joe Mirra & Tim Ryan: Simpson Court Mural Update 43 
Mr. Mirra and Mr. Ryan provided an update on ongoing efforts to incorporate additional public art 44 
into downtown Wallingford, including ‘Mark Gingras Mural Project’ at 50 North Main Street, next 45 
to Half Moon Café. They explained that Mark had a passion for Wallingford and was always 46 
looking for opportunities for enhancement.  After his passing, Mr. Ryan, Mr. Mirra and others 47

worked alongside Mark’s family and the ‘Mark Gingras Liberty Bank Community Fund’ which was 48 
created to honor him as the former Liberty Bank Board Chairman and Wallingford resident and 49 
Wallingford Arts and Cultural Alliance (WACA), to continue honoring his memory through 50 
community leadership and philanthropic spirit. Mr. Mirra and Mr. Ryan noted that a Ribbon 51 
Cutting was held May 2026 for the ‘Mark Gingras Mural Project’ which was created by the 52 
accomplished muralist Ryan Christenson, better known as ARCY, who is a proud Sheehan High 53 
School graduate. They explained artwork for a second alley is being considered, with completion 54 
anticipated in the spring. Mr. Mirra and Mr. Ryan noted there may be other projects in the future. 55 
The group further discussed the importance of maintaining and promoting a vibrant, walkable 56 
downtown. Mr. Ryan emphasized downtown’s competitive advantage and encouraged EDC to 57 
continue supporting beautification efforts and identifying opportunities to enhance the area, 58 
including the historic train station. 59 
Chairman Bracale discussed the EDC’s previous RFP for the train station, which was 60 
unsuccessful. The Commission discussed lessons learned from the prior process and the 61 
importance of establishing a clear vision for the property before issuing another RFP. Members 62 
expressed interest in involving Town Council representatives and other stakeholders earlier in 63 
the process 64 
Additionally, Mr. Mirra discussed the potential benefits of outdoor dining to the downtown 65 
experience.  He noted that it creates destination appeal by attracting visitors and regional 66 
tourists, driving retail foot traffic, fostering a strong sense of community and excitement, and 67 
creating social hubs where people can celebrate milestones, hold meetings, and build 68 
neighborhood camaraderie. 69 
Mr. Crouch recognized Mr. Mirra, Mr. Ryan and others for their ongoing commitment and 70 
continued efforts to improve downtown and noted Wallingford’s improved standing with 71 
Connecticut Main Street as a result of all of the enhancements that have been made. 72 
b. Dale Kroop, REX Development: ‘On the Ground – Roles and Responsibilities of the 73 
Town’s “economic development team” & strategic planning for development’ 74 
Dale Kroop of REX Development introduced himself and provided an overview of economic 75 
development activities and resources. He discussed business retention and expansion, business 76 
attraction, sector-based economic development, marketing and storytelling, signage, grant 77 
opportunities, and business visitation as important components of an EDC’s work. 78 
 79 
Mr. Kroop emphasized the importance of understanding the needs of both large and small 80 
businesses through regular business visits. He also discussed the emerging concept of 81 
“greyfields,” referring to properties such as former schools, bowling alleys, gyms, and strip malls 82 
that have outlived their original use. State funding may be available for feasibility studies, cost-83 
benefit analyses, and redevelopment of these properties. The train station could potentially be 84 
identified as a greyfield project. 85 
 86 
Mr. Kroop also discussed opportunities to connect manufacturers, healthcare organizations, 87 
workforce partners, and the EDC to address workforce needs. Housing availability and 88 
affordability were identified as important factors in attracting and retaining employees and 89 
businesses.  90 
 91 
Mr. Kroop described workforce initiatives designed to expose students and parents to career 92 
opportunities in the trades, manufacturing, STEM, construction, automotive fields, and other 93 
technical careers. He suggested that EDC could consider workshops bringing manufacturers and 94 
parents together to discuss career opportunities, salaries, and available pathways. 95

through educational workshops covering the fundamentals of starting and operating a business. 98 
Mr. Kroop noted that he could assist EDC with developing programming and connecting 99 
appropriate speakers or panelists. 100

Development staff and the Administration. Commissioners agreed that the EDC would benefit 103 
from a workshop and development of a work plan identifying priorities and measurable goals. Mr. 104 
Kroop suggested that a workshop could focus on a specific project, such as the train station, as a 105 
way to establish a collaborative working model.   Commissioners also discussed clarifying the 106 
EDC’s role, improving communication with Town officials, breaking down silos, and ensuring the 107

6. Old Business: 164 
Review of Current Incentives and Next Steps 165 
The Commission discussed the current economic development incentives and the need to review and 166 
renew existing programs. Commissioners discussed the challenges associated with incentive housing 167 
zones and whether similar programs in other communities have been effective.  Mr. Crouch noted he 168 
could provide examples of other towns’ plans. Commissioners discussed keeping incentive programs 169 
simple and recognizing that individual projects may require customized approaches rather than a one-170 
size-fits-all model. It was also noted that taxes are only one component of a broader incentive package 171 
that may include utilities and other factors.   Mr. Crouch and Commissioners Bracale, Lombardi and 172 
McAnnenny will continue reviewing this topic and provide more information at a later date.  173
